decisions.reason: Archiving software with its own website page signals a prominent, low-cost offering that complements the firm's control business, so there is no shortfall against aspirations that would trigger search for other uses of its resources.

This second archiving and reporting tool overlaps with Product A and is only mentioned on the website, which makes it a candidate for consolidation, but carrying software costs little and slack lets the firm wait for clearer results.
The safety manhole door has its own page and fits the core water-engineering hardware business, so it likely meets aspirations and should be kept.
The floating sludge extractor is close to the firm's core tank equipment and is only mentioned, so its results are still uncertain, but they do not fall short enough to justify dropping it.
Control technology for its own machinery supports the established business and customer retention, so dropping it would bring little benefit.
